name: Marine predatory fish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish)
scope_note: Marine predatory finfish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish), fresh or frozen, edible portion. Lead binds the predatory tuna/bonito 200 line; total mercury binds the EU higher-mercury-fish 1000 ceiling (not the general 500). MeHg is bounded by tHg. Total chromium binds HK fish 1000. Ni and Al are screened (no sovereign ML); Sn and Cr-VI are not-material. Canned predatory fish route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

Pb.basis: edible portion, wet weight. Predatory-fish-specific lead: Costa Rica RTCR 409:2008 sets tuna/bonito Pb 200 (stricter than the EU general fish-muscle 300, retained as concurring context).

Cd.basis: edible portion, wet weight. General fish-muscle cadmium 50 (the strictest sovereign floor); the higher predatory-species carve-outs (tuna 100, swordfish 300) are looser and not adopted, so certification holds predatory fish to the general 50.

tAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic. Strictest sovereign fish total-As is 1000 (Paraguay/Singapore/Israel concur).

iAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic. EU Reg. 2025/1891 muscle-meat-of-fish (other) iAs 100, HK Cap 132V fish iAs 100 concur.

tHg.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Predatory species (tuna, swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel) bind the EU 2023/915 higher-mercury-fish ceiling of 1000; the general 500 does not apply to these listed higher-mercury species.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of total mercury and is arithmetically bounded by it (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling for predatory fish (1000) is equal to or stricter than the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML for predatory fish (MX/PH/TT/TH/US predatory MeHg 1000), so passing tHg guarantees MeHg compliance and no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation is optional and cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg predatory-fish ceiling (EU 2023/915, 1000); no sovereign MeHg ML sits below it
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU; US-FDA; MX; PH; TT; TH; GSO; HK

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for fish or fishery products anywhere in the register or (audit-verified) worldwide — EU 2024/1987 nickel covers plant foods and seaweed only, not animal seafood. Nickel is screened rather than assigned an invented or mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign fish/fishery Ni ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: Fresh/frozen predatory fish has no tinplate contact; inorganic tin is a can-migration analyte. A full register Sn sweep (audit-affirmed 2026-08-14) shows every seafood tin ML is canned/tinplate-migration scope or a canned 'any food' catch-all at the ~250 mg/kg migration ceiling; no sovereign sets a non-canned fish tin matrix limit. If the product is canned it is certified under the canned-seafood subcategory tin limit.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to the canned-seafood Sn limit if packaged in tinplate.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No non-canned fish Sn ML; canned-seafood Sn limits are can-only
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: Codex CXS 193; EU; US-FDA; MX; CR; HK

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for seafood in any checked jurisdiction (the only register 'all food' aluminium row, China 100000, is an aluminium-ADDITIVE use limit, not a contaminant ML, and does not apply). Aluminium in fish is background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level. Screened rather than aligned to a non-existent ML.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML to align to.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total chromium. Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates total chromium in fish at 1.0 mg/kg (1000); the only other on-scope sovereign (India FSSAI all-fishery-products 12000) is 12x looser and not adopted.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which binds at 1000 for fish. No jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level, and in a reducing animal-tissue matrix Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so there is no chromate pathway in fish (unlike lead-chromate-adulterated spices). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in fish.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (HK fish 1000)
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)
